requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority on node1 named “OS Comparison Root CA”.
requirements.summary: The executor created a self-signed CA certificate with the exact common name, critical CA and signing constraints, a SHA-256 signature, and a matching valid RSA-3072 private key. The CA key and passphrase are root-owned with restrictive permissions.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority.
requirements.summary: The certificate was installed in the RHEL trust-anchor directory, appeared as an authority anchor, and passed default OpenSSL verification. A CA-issued TLS server certificate was also accepted by both OpenSSL and curl using system-default trust.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were unchanged from baseline through final collection. The only installed utility was the matching RHEL 10 OpenSSL 3.2.2 package, aligned with the already-installed OpenSSL libraries.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through disconnection, the post-restart boot identity changed, services and trust recovered, CA data persisted, and post-restart TLS validation succeeded. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear task or evidence roles: installing compatible OpenSSL tooling, creating the CA, installing/rebuilding system trust, bounded TLS validation, and the mandatory restart protocol. Temporary certificates, keys, logs, listeners, and directories from the TLS tests—including the initially unsuccessful test—were removed; no unnecessary mutation remained or was identified. Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, no extra listening sockets, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-related temporary-file/PID changes.
